Phase 32 plan submitted: docs/phases/orchestration-controls-usage-surfacing-30-arc.md (brief: docs/tagteam-3.0-proposal.md §4 Phase 32, §8 Q4). Branch: phase-32-orchestration-controls (PR at the end).

Scope: `tagteam pause/resume/cancel-turn` (pause honored by ALL watcher modes; cancel kills the in-flight headless turn and the engine labels the outcome `cancelled` via a stem-matched marker), `tagteam interject` (additive `interjections` table with provenance — by/ts/phase/type/round/turn + delivered_role/round/stem/ts stamped only when the receiving headless turn is `ok`; injected as an ARBITER INTERJECTIONS block in the composed prompt; surfaced to interactive agents via an additive `interjections` list on `cycle rounds` output; rounds JSONL/table untouched), `tagteam usage` (per-turn lines + by-role/by-cycle/totals, `--json`, this project only), cross-platform `notify()` (osascript / PowerShell toast with `msg` fallback / notify-send; `TAGTEAM_NO_NOTIFY`; `watcher.notify_macos` kept as alias so existing patches work), Phase 31 follow-ups closed from data: `--turn-retries N` with a deterministic at-least-once rule (retry only spawn_failed/nonzero_exit/timeout AND `git status --porcelain` hash unchanged since pre-spawn; never no_round/cancelled), per-role `headless.timeout_minutes`, trimmed-contract question closed as "keep full" (contract ≈4–5K tokens vs 282K–1.69M per real reviewer turn, 91–96% cache-read). Optional `tagteam rollback X.Y.Z` (print-only unless --yes; detects uv-tool vs pip). Schema v4 additive (interjections table, `cancelled` status). Release 0.9.0.

Four open questions with recommendations: resume auto re-dispatch once; `--to lead|reviewer` targeting for interjections; toast-then-msg on Windows accepted as best-effort; keep rollback in.

Dogfood: THIS plan cycle's reviewer turns run headless (closes Phase 31 finding 9(b)); impl cycle exercises pause/interject/usage on this repo and cancel-turn on a scratch turn. Please review against docs/checklists/plan_review.md.

The plan is well structured and aligned with Phase 32, but three blocking changes are needed before implementation.

1. Make the retry gate safe with respect to both repository and handoff state. Hashing only `git status --porcelain` is insufficient: a turn can successfully run `cycle add` in DB-backed storage (handoff-state.json and .tagteam are ignored), then exit nonzero, and the proposed loop would retry the already-completed owed turn. A commit can also change HEAD while leaving status clean, and the default status output can collapse an untracked directory so edits beneath it do not change the hash. Snapshot and compare the expected cycle/state identity (at minimum state seq plus target cycle entry/status), and never retry after any handoff transition. The repository fingerprint should include HEAD plus `git status --porcelain=v1 -z --untracked-files=all`. Add tests for: nonzero after a successful cycle write (no retry), commit-then-fail (no retry), and mutation inside an already-untracked directory (no retry). Keep `no_round` and `cancelled` non-retryable as planned.

2. Specify stale-inflight safety for `cancel-turn`. Reading a leftover inflight.json and calling a public `kill_pid_tree(pid)` can kill an unrelated process after PID reuse, especially after a watcher crash. Define process-identity/liveness validation before signaling (implementation choice, but it must bind the PID to the recorded watcher/turn), reject missing/self/watcher/unrelated PIDs, and clean or report stale metadata without killing. Add an acceptance test whose stale inflight file points at an unrelated sleeper and proves it remains alive; retain the live child/grandchild kill test.

3. Resolve the interjection API in the normative plan. I accept the recommendation to ship `--to lead|reviewer`, defaulting to the next role, but `target_role` currently appears only in Open Question 2 and is absent from the in-scope command, schema, DB accessors, files, and success criteria. Add the column and validation, define pending selection as untargeted-or-matching the receiving role, and ensure delivery stamps exactly the IDs included in that prompt (not all currently pending rows). Cover a targeted note waiting across the other role's successful turn, then being delivered and stamped on its target role's turn. Also define `interject` behavior when there is no active owed cycle.

The other recommendations are accepted: resume auto-redispatches exactly once, Windows notification remains best-effort toast then msg fallback, and the small rollback command stays in scope. Please fold all four decisions into the normative Scope/Technical Approach/Schema/Success Criteria so implementation does not depend on an unresolved Open Questions section.

Round 2: all three blocking items folded into the normative Scope / Technical Approach / Schema / Success Criteria; the Open Questions section is now "None blocking" with a Decisions list (your four accepted recommendations + the two new rulings).

1. Retry gate — now gated on BOTH fingerprints, snapshotted pre-spawn: repo = sha1(`git rev-parse HEAD` ‖ `git status --porcelain=v1 -z --untracked-files=all`) (HEAD catches commit-then-fail; untracked-files=all catches edits under an already-untracked dir), and handoff = (state.seq, target cycle entry count, cycle state/ready_for/round). Retry only if outcome ∈ {spawn_failed, nonzero_exit, timeout} AND both unchanged; any handoff transition ⇒ never retry; no_round/cancelled never retried; non-git ⇒ only spawn_failed (handoff fingerprint still checked). Criteria/tests enumerate: nonzero after a successful cycle add → no retry; commit-then-fail → no retry; mutation inside an already-untracked directory → no retry; tracked edit → no retry; clean nonzero → retried.

2. cancel-turn stale-inflight safety — inflight.json now records `watcher_pid` (engine's os.getpid()) and `started_at`. Before signalling: reject pid missing / == self / == watcher_pid; reject not-alive; require parent_pid(pid) == watcher_pid (POSIX `ps -o ppid=`, Windows Get-CimInstance; lookup failure ⇒ unverifiable ⇒ do NOT kill); additionally reject start_time < started_at where cheap. On rejection: print reason, remove the stale inflight.json (metadata only, nothing signalled), exit 1. New small `tagteam/procs.py` (pid_alive/parent_pid/process_start_time). Acceptance test: hand-written inflight pointing at an unrelated sleeper (parent ≠ recorded watcher_pid) → sleeper stays alive, file cleaned, exit 1; plus self/watcher/missing/dead/unverifiable cases; the live child+grandchild kill test retained.

3. Interjection API — `--to lead|reviewer` is now in the in-scope command, schema (`target_role TEXT CHECK (NULL or lead|reviewer)`), accessors (`add_interjection(..., target_role)`, `pending_interjections_for(role)` = undelivered AND (target_role IS NULL OR = role), `mark_interjections_delivered(ids, …)` exact ids), files, prompt block (shows target), delivery rule (engine retains the exact rendered ids and stamps only those on `ok`; mid-turn or other-role notes stay pending), and success criteria (a `--to reviewer` note written before a lead turn is absent from the lead prompt and undelivered after the lead's ok, then present + stamped on the reviewer's ok). No active owed cycle: note stored (phase/type/round from state if any, turn NULL) with a warning "delivered to the next turn that starts".

Decisions recorded: resume auto-redispatches exactly once; toast then msg best-effort; rollback stays in scope (print-only unless --yes).

The round-1 concerns are substantially addressed, but three blocking edge cases remain in the normative design.

1. Make the repository retry fingerprint content-sensitive. `HEAD + git status --porcelain=v1 -z --untracked-files=all` identifies path/status changes, not all tree-content changes. If a tracked file is already modified before spawn and the agent edits it again, the porcelain bytes remain ` M <path>`; likewise, modifying the contents of an already-present untracked file leaves the porcelain bytes unchanged. The loop can therefore retry over agent work despite claiming that any tree change prevents retry. Define a fingerprint over actual tracked/index/worktree content plus untracked path/content (for example, HEAD plus content-sensitive staged/unstaged diff material and hashes of untracked entries), while retaining deterministic ordering and non-git behavior. Add tests where (a) a pre-existing modified tracked file is edited again and (b) a pre-existing untracked file's contents are edited; both must suppress retry. Update the risk text, which currently limits the accepted blind spot to gitignored files.

2. Finish the process-identity binding for `cancel-turn`. Parent PID equality plus `child_start >= inflight.started_at` does not identify the recorded processes after PID reuse: after a watcher crash, reused watcher/child PIDs necessarily have newer start times and can pass that inequality. It can also reject a legitimate POSIX child if `ps -o lstart=` rounds to seconds while `started_at` has subsecond precision. Record and validate stable creation identities for both watcher and child (or use an equivalently safe watcher-mediated/native-handle design), with explicit timestamp resolution/tolerance if timestamps are used; reject an identity mismatch before signaling. Add a mocked acceptance/unit case where the numeric child and parent PIDs match the stale metadata but one recorded creation identity does not, proving no kill occurs. Keep the unrelated-sleeper and live tree-kill tests.

3. Define interjection consumption across interactive/headless mode changes. Interactive `cycle rounds` surfaces a note but deliberately leaves `delivered_ts` NULL, while `pending_interjections_for(role)` is currently global apart from role. Consequently, every historical interactive interjection remains pending and can be injected into an unrelated future headless turn, phase, or cycle. Specify eligibility/retirement semantics that preserve the required mid-turn and targeted-across-other-role behavior without replaying already-surfaced historical notes. Add a test that creates/surfaces an interjection during an interactive cycle, advances the cycle, then starts a later headless turn and proves the old note is not injected; also cover the intended same-cycle mode-switch behavior explicitly.

Once these are folded into Scope, Technical Approach, accessors/schema as needed, risks, and Success Criteria, the plan should be ready to approve.

Round 3: the three r2 edge cases folded into Scope / Technical Approach / Schema / accessors / Risks / Success Criteria; Decisions list extended (items 6–8 marked r2).

1. Content-sensitive repo fingerprint — sha1(`git rev-parse HEAD` ‖ `git write-tree` of the real index ‖ `git write-tree` of a temporary index built with `GIT_INDEX_FILE=<tmp> git read-tree HEAD && git add -A`). Git hashes the bytes of every tracked and non-ignored untracked path, so editing an already-modified tracked file, changing an already-present untracked file's contents, or a stage-only `git add` all change it; ordering is git's own; temp index removed; only .gitignored paths remain outside (Risk text rewritten accordingly, and the handoff fingerprint independently guards .tagteam/). Tests/criteria add: edit-of-already-modified tracked file, content change of pre-existing untracked file, stage-only add — all suppress retry.

2. Process identity — inflight.json now records `child_ident` and `watcher_ident` captured AT SPAWN via `procs.identity(pid)` = "<pid>:<creation-time-string>" straight from the platform tool (POSIX `ps -o lstart=` / Linux /proc starttime ticks; Windows Win32_Process CreationDate), or None. cancel-turn recomputes both with the same helper and requires STRING EQUALITY (same source both sides ⇒ no >=, no tolerance, no rounding issue), plus parent_pid == watcher_pid, plus not-self/not-watcher/alive; None on either side ⇒ unverifiable ⇒ no kill; reused watcher/child pids after a crash have different creation strings ⇒ rejected. Criteria add the mocked case: numeric pids match the metadata but child_ident OR watcher_ident differs ⇒ no kill; engine records both identities at spawn; unrelated-sleeper and live tree-kill tests retained.

3. Interjection eligibility — cycle-scoped: pending_interjections_for(role, phase, type) = undelivered AND unretired AND (target NULL or = role) AND ((phase,type) == receiving turn's target cycle OR phase IS NULL — the "nothing owed" case, eligible once for the next cycle's first turn). Notes for other cycles or terminal cycles are never injected ⇒ no replay of historical interactive notes into unrelated headless turns. Same-cycle mode switch is explicit and intended: injected once with the caveat "may already have been addressed in earlier rounds; verify". Added `retired_ts/retired_by` (additive) with `tagteam interject --list` / `--retire ID` (append-only otherwise). Criteria add the cross-cycle no-replay test, the same-cycle mode-switch test, the NULL-phase once test, and list/retire.

Round 3 resolves the previously requested content-sensitive retry, PID-identity, and cycle-scoping designs in substance, but two normative contradictions/safety gaps still block approval.

1. Make the no-active-cycle interjection rule internally consistent. Scope currently says that when state exists but is not owed (for example `done`), the row keeps `phase/type/round` from that terminal state and only `turn` is NULL, while eligibility admits only the receiving `(phase,type)` or `phase IS NULL`. Such a note is therefore scoped to the old terminal cycle and can never satisfy the warning that it will be delivered to the next cycle. Technical Approach instead says NULL phase/turn, and Success Criteria alternates between NULL turn and a NULL-phase test. Pick one implementable rule and use it everywhere. The simplest is to set `phase/type/round/turn` all NULL whenever there is no active owed turn (optionally preserve the observed terminal identity in separate provenance fields if needed), then define “next” as the first *eligible* turn so `--to reviewer` can wait across a lead turn. Add the specific test: terminal state for cycle A → interject → start cycle B → note is injected/stamped on B's first role-eligible successful turn, not stranded on A.

2. Close the remaining retry-fingerprint safety cases or narrow the guarantee. The temporary-index `git add -A` tree does not hash dirty content inside a tracked submodule; a pre-existing dirty submodule can be edited again while the superproject HEAD, real index tree, and temporary-index tree all remain unchanged. It can also fail on legitimate repository states such as an unmerged index, but the plan does not define a fail-closed result. This contradicts “only `.gitignore`d paths remain outside” and can retry over agent work. Include deterministic recursive submodule content/state in the fingerprint (with a pre-dirty-edit test), and specify that any fingerprint initialization/recomputation failure or unsupported repository state makes the attempt non-retryable. Alternatively explicitly make repositories with submodules/index states the safe fail-closed path; do not silently use the unchanged-tree retry rule there.

With those points aligned across Scope, Technical Approach/accessors, Risks, and Success Criteria, the plan should be ready to approve.
